recommended.title: Auth integration decision
recommended.notes: ALLOWEDPATHS BOTH NARROWED AND WIDENED, AND THE WIDENING IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. As declared, this task reserved docs/**, apps/web/src/** and packages/contracts/** -- all twenty-one documents, the entire web application and the whole contracts package -- for a decision record. Each of those three prefix-contains an active task's write surface, so a P0 that is already finished in the tree could not be claimed by anyone. Worse, and in the opposite direction, packages/auth/** was NOT declared at all, yet nine files there are this task's primary output: a reconcile-existing run would have reported the bulk of its own implementation as outside its surface. Both errors come from declaring a surface by guess before the work exists rather than from reading it afterwards. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS ALREADY IN THE TREE and only the control-plane record lags, the same pattern as PL-0204, PL-0205 and PL-0601. All four acceptance clauses are met: packages/auth exports the seam at . and ./server with better-auth a dependency of that package alone; sessions are database-backed through @better-auth/drizzle-adapter and packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql; packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts carries ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES with findSurfaceViolations defaulting unknown plugins to violations; and both better-auth and its adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1 with no caret, asserted by enabled-surface.test.ts against REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. The decision itself is ADR-007 in docs/DECISIONS.md, which self-labels Proposed because claude-lead wrote it and WAS also this task's reviewAgent when it was written -- that is no longer true, see the reviewAgent change below, and the label should be revisited by whoever closes this task. TWO HONEST CAVEATS STATED IN THE ADR RATHER THAN HIDDEN, and neither is an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed against a database, because there is no PostgreSQL anywhere in this environment; and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. PROVENANCE: this must be started with --reconcile-existing, not against HEAD. The probe is packages/auth/src/enabled-surface.ts -- but after the PL-0205 finding, a filename probe is not enough on its own: whoever reconciles it must confirm the candidate base tree contains neither ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES nor WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES anywhere, so a file created by a later move cannot open the range after the behaviour it claims to cover. REVIEWAGENT MOVED FROM claude-lead TO gpt-architect. This task carries a security-review gate on an authentication boundary, and its decision record was written by claude-lead. A reviewer that is also the author is not a reviewer; routing it outward makes the review stricter rather than looser, which is the only direction this may be changed in. THE MIGRATION IS A REVIEWDEPENDENCY, AND THE REVIEWER MADE THAT A CONDITION OF CLAIMING. It observed that this record cites packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql as the factual basis for the database-backed-session clause while the file sat in no part of the declared surface, and gave two defensible resolutions and one forbidden one: add it as a reviewDependency, or stop using it as evidence and let the Drizzle adapter and configuration carry the clause alone -- but do not mix the two. Its words: either is defensible; mixing the two is not. Resolved as a reviewDependency, because the ADR genuinely does rest on it: ADR-007 argues database-backed sessions over stateless ones partly on the shape of that migration, and an approval that did not fingerprint it could stay fresh after the schema underneath the argument changed. It is deliberately NOT an allowedPath -- this task did not write it, PL-0402 did, and reviewDependencies exist precisely so a boundary a task depends on can be reviewed without being reserved. No collision follows: reviewDependencies reserve nothing, so PL-0402 may still declare packages/persistence/** as a write surface whenever it is claimed.
recommended.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam that the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range

recommended.title: A real catalog metadata source
recommended.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
recommended.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.
